text:
Sam: Heads-up: RateScale sent invoice RS-2026-04 for $27,450. Looks like we hit an overage plus a misapplied renewal fee. Link: https://ratescale.example/invoices/RS-2026-04
Priya: Can you paste the invoice summary + PO and contract id? cc @Ellen from finance.
Sam: Lines:
```
Item: RateScale pilot usage Feb 2026 - $5,900
Item: RateScale committed tier renewal Mar 2026 - $18,000
Item: RateScale overage (mar-01 to mar-07) - $3,550
Tax: $0
Total: $27,450
PO: PO-110020
Contract: CT-2025-RS
```
Ellen: Finance: we prefer credit notes rather than refunds for small disputes. If vendor issues credit note we can apply to next invoice; if >$10k need AP hold. Also need GL mapping.
Sam: The overage is from a reproducible benchmark run (run-id: bench-2045). Not prod. I can attach logs and the query to show it was scheduled.
procurement-bot: Ticket created TKT-6122 "RateScale invoice: overage + renewal misapply" assigned to Priya. SLA 72h.
Priya: Proposed ask to RateScale: (1) credit the pilot amount $5,900 (pilot overlap), (2) waive the $3,550 overage as one-time courtesy given it's benchmarking, (3) amend contract to add an automated alert threshold for overages and move billing to quarterly in-arrears starting 2026-07-01. Vendor to issue credit note >= $9,450. Procurement will accept credit note in lieu of refund if legal signs amendment.
VendorRep: Thanks for the details. I see invoice generated automatically on renewal cycle. I can push this to billing and request a credit note; need written confirmation of the benchmark run and PO for our records. Can we also discuss moving to a flat tier price for the March pilot-month anomaly?
Ellen: We can provide the benchmark log and a short attestation. Finance agrees to credit note but needs it dated within the current quarter. Also, any new flat-tier pricing must be priced vs committed volume.
Priya: Let's propose two options to RateScale: (A) one-off credit note $9,450 + cadence change to quarterly-in-arrears (preferred), OR (B) immediate credit of pilot amount + a 20% discount on next quarter if we sign a 6mo committed capacity addendum. Which do you prefer? cc @legal for amendment drafting.
legal: We'll draft a short amendment template for quarterly billing + overage alerting; include credit-note acceptance clause. Send contract ref CT-2025-RS and proposed effective date and we'll redline.
VendorRep: I'll escalate. Expect a response by EOD tomorrow. If they accept option B, we may ask for revenue recognition impact details for your accounting team.
Ellen: Noted. If option B is chosen, finance needs forecast numbers and commit thresholds. Sam: can you run a 6-week usage projection?
Sam: On it. I'll attach projection and the benchmark logs to TKT-6122. Target close date Apr 20 to avoid manual reconciliations.
Priya: Owners: @Sam (usage evidence), @Priya (vendor negotiation), @Ellen (finance sign-off), @legal (contract amendment).
